title: Images, video and HTML surfaces
summary: Place images, video and HTML content in a scene and account for their loading and update behavior.

blocks.text: RTImage and RTVideo expose media on Model-based 3D surfaces. MeshSprite maps texture/video data onto vector geometry with UV generation, which is useful for nonlinear deformations. VideoData manages the HTML video object and playback synchronization; SpriteFragment can sample external video textures.

Videos need to be ready before capture. In offline mode the engine advances or seeks the video to the scene frame time and waits for frames, rather than assuming real-time media playback is synchronized. Browser media decoding and autoplay permissions still apply.

RTHTML offers supported browser-native HTML texture paths and a CSS3D DOM overlay fallback. The texture modes rely on capabilities that may be experimental in the current browser; CSS3D uses a positioned DOM surface and has different capture behavior. Iframes and interactive forms are particularly dependent on the selected path.

A DOM overlay that looks correct in the live page is not automatically part of a GPU framebuffer snapshot. Verify the selected mode in the actual export workflow. Pointer forwarding raycasts the 3D plane, converts to local DOM coordinates and dispatches supported interactions.

Dispose video playback, object URLs, DOM surfaces and texture resources when removing a host. Share a media source intentionally when several surfaces use it; source lifetime and entity lifetime are not necessarily the same.
One image asset is loaded and displayed at an explicit scene size.
